BIO-key Q3 Software License Fees Grew 39%, Its Third Consecutive Quarter of Double-Digit Growth, Driven Primarily by Momentum in the Middle East and Europe;

Hosts Call Today at 10am ET

 

Holmdel, NJ – November 13, 2026 – BIO-key® International, Inc. (Nasdaq: BKYI), a global leader in Identity and Access Management (IAM) and biometric authentication technologies, today announced its third quarter (Q3’26) and nine-month (9M’26) results for the period ended September 30, 2026. BIO-key will host an investor call today at 10:00am ET (details below).

 

Financial Highlights

 

●

Q3’26 license fee revenue rose 39% to $1.3M, reflecting continued growth in its base of annual recurring software revenue. BIO-key has delivered meaningful year-over-year software license fee growth in each of the last three quarters.

 

●

Q3’26 total revenues were $1.48M vs. $1.55M in Q3’25, as license fee growth largely offset lower hardware and service revenues, which have greater variability due to the timing of projects.

 

●

Q3’26 gross margin improved to 90% vs. 77% in Q3’25, reflecting the increase in high-margin license fees as a percentage of total revenue. BIO-key’s blended gross margin has increased for five consecutive quarters, from 73% in Q2’25 to 90% in Q3’26, reflecting both new customer deployments and its expanding base of annual recurring software license fees.

 

●

Q3’26 net loss narrowed 8% to $(886K) vs. $(965K) in Q3’25.

 

●

9M’26 revenues grew 14% to $5.5M, gross margin improved to 86% from 77%, and net loss improved 42% to $(1.7M) vs. $(2.9M) in 9M’25.

 

●

Working capital improved to $3.1M at the close of Q3’26, from $1.4M at year-end 2025.

 

●

BIO-key retired its remaining note in Q3’26.

 

Business Outlook

 

●

BIO-key anticipates a solid finish to 2026 and a strong start to 2027, supported by recent Middle East government wins, a growing pipeline of government and financial sector opportunities, expanding deployments with existing customers, and anticipated annual license renewals.

 

Recent Progress

 

●

Middle East: BIO-key added three new government customers in October, bringing to eight the number of new Middle East region customers in the past seven months:

 

–

Middle East government security agency customer

 

–

Middle East government contract for passwordless, biometric IAM solutions

 

–

New customer within a Middle East government’s national security ecosystem

 

–

Partnership with Al Majlis Group to expand identity security across the Arabian Gulf

 

●

Portugal: Integration of BIO-key’s IAM and biometric authentication solutions into the cybersecurity portfolio of Cipher, a Prosegur company, starting in Portugal – with plans to explore extending the offering to other Cipher markets, including Spain, the U.S. and Brazil.

 

●

Agentic AI: BIO-key received FIDO Alliance full certification for its Passkey:YOU™ authentication, opening markets where phones are restricted and supporting biometric approval of AI agent actions.

 

 

BIO-key CEO, Mike DePasquale commented, “Our Q3’26 results reflect the building strength of our core software business. Software license fee revenue grew 39% in Q3’26, offsetting variability in our more episodic hardware and services revenue and lifting gross margin to 90% from 77% a year ago. Supported largely by growth in high-margin software licenses, BIO-key’s gross margin has improved each quarter since Q2’25. Despite modestly lower Q3’26 revenue, we successfully narrowed our net loss in the quarter, and for the first nine months of 2026. Year to date we have grown revenue by 14%, reduced our net loss by 42% and we retired our remaining note outstanding leaving us effectively debt free.

 

“The real story, however, is the customers who are choosing BIO-key, such as the Central Bank of Jordan which has selected us to help them launch a national biometric authentication initiative to modernize financial sector access to digital services. Separately, a Portuguese national security agency chose our identity platform to protect some of its most sensitive systems. Additionally, we recently added three more Middle East government customers, including a security agency that went from first meeting to agreement in less than two months, bringing us to eight new Middle East region customers in recent months. Governments and banks set the highest bar for identity security, and their decision to trust BIO-key to their most sensitive environments is the strongest possible validation of our company and our solutions.

 

“Our momentum across Europe, the Middle East and Africa reflects the investment we have made in developing regional teams and a strong network of channel partners who know these markets and customers. Our partner network is increasingly bringing opportunities to us, shortening our sales cycles and extending our reach into new countries and sectors. That momentum is showing up in our results: third quarter revenue from our Europe, Middle East and South America region grew 39%, as license fees from the region more than doubled.

 

“Looking forward, the growth of artificial intelligence is also presenting opportunities as the growing commercial prevalence of AI agents creates a new identity challenge. Industry research suggests that machine identities, including AI agents, already outnumber human identities by more than 100 to 1. To address this trend, the FIDO Alliance began developing standards for trusted AI agent interactions, centered on verifying who authorized an agent’s action and within what limits. We believe the answer has to be a verified human, not a password nor a device. With FIDO certification of Passkey:YOU, our Identity-Bound Biometrics can tie the approval of sensitive AI-driven actions to the actual person accountable for them, which we see as a meaningful new market opportunity alongside our core workforce and customer authentication business.

 

“Our recent wins and a growing pipeline of government and banking opportunities across EMEA position us for a strong finish to 2026. More importantly, we believe the foundation we are building today, with marquee government and financial customers, growing high-margin software revenue, a streamlined cost structure and a cleaner balance sheet, sets the stage for an exciting 2027.”

 

Financial Review

Total revenues were $1,482,781 in Q3’26 compared to $1,549,706 in Q3’25. License fee revenues increased 39% to $1,275,249 vs. $917,951 in Q3’25, reflecting several new customer deployments, and represented 86% of total revenues vs. 59% in Q3’25. Revenues from BIO-key’s EMESA region (Europe, Middle East and South America) increased 39% to $924,760, as EMESA license fee revenues more than doubled to $903,249 from $446,480 in Q3’25. For 9M’26, total revenues increased 14% to $5,548,305 vs. $4,853,772 in 9M’25, driven by a 37% increase in license fee revenues to $3,870,487.

 

 

Q3’26 hardware revenues were $12,404 vs. $363,642 in Q3’25, as new customer orders in Q3’26 were primarily software-only, while Q3’25 reflected a large hardware deployment by a long-term customer and expanded hardware deployments by several existing customers. Service, maintenance and other revenues decreased 27% to $195,128 in Q3’26 vs. $268,113 in Q3’25, primarily reflecting the timing of service agreement renewals and the steady shift in BIO-key’s business to Partner-led Software-as-a-Service and subscription deployments.

 

Q3’26 gross profit increased 12% to $1,339,408 from $1,191,718 in Q3’25, and gross margin improved to 90% vs. 77% in Q3’25, reflecting the higher mix of high-margin license fee revenue. For 9M’26, gross profit increased 27% to $4,782,681 vs. $3,752,106 in 9M’25, and gross margin improved to 86% from 77%.

 

BIO-key’s Q3’26 operating expenses increased 4% to $2,159,621 from $2,083,908 in Q3’25. Sequentially, operating expenses decreased 2% from $2,203,445 in Q2’26, including a 2% decrease in selling, general and administrative expenses. Selling, general and administrative expenses increased 9% to $1,524,583, reflecting higher administrative personnel costs and costs related to the Company’s annual meeting, while research, development and engineering expenses decreased 7% to $635,038, primarily reflecting lower personnel costs. For 9M’26, operating expenses decreased 1% to $6,290,013 from $6,368,784 in 9M’25.

 

Reflecting higher gross profit, BIO-key’s Q3’26 operating loss improved to $(820,213) from $(892,190) in Q3’25, and its net loss improved to $(886,083) from $(964,849) in Q3’25. Including a non-cash deemed dividend of $4,502,004 related to the August warrant inducement, net loss available to common stockholders was $(5,388,087), or $(4.01) per share, compared to $(964,849), or $(1.44) per share, in Q3’25, as the deemed dividend more than offset the smaller net loss. Weighted average common shares outstanding (basic and diluted) were 1,342,766 in Q3’26 and 671,820 in Q3’25. Per share amounts and weighted average common shares outstanding reflect the 1-for-10 reverse split effective April 30, 2026.

 

Also reflecting higher revenue and gross profit and lower operating expenses, BIO-key’s 9M’26 net loss improved 42% to $(1,667,972) from $(2,868,790) in 9M’25. Including the non-cash deemed dividend, net loss available to common stockholders was $(6,169,976), or $(5.37) per share, compared to $(2,868,790), or $(4.87) per share, in 9M’25.

 

Balance Sheet

BIO-key’s stockholders’ equity improved to $6,541,642 at September 30, 2026, compared to $4,334,878 at June 30, 2026 and $5,106,805 at December 31, 2025, reflecting the benefit of $2.5M in gross proceeds from a warrant inducement transaction completed in August.

 

As of September 30, 2026, BIO-key had $5.3M of current assets, including $2.2M of cash and cash equivalents, $2.4M of accounts receivable and $0.4M of inventory. Working capital improved to $3.1M at September 30, 2026 from $0.8M at June 30, 2026 and $1.4M at December 31, 2025.

 

During Q3, BIO-key retired the remaining balance of its note payable, through exchanges for common stock leaving the company effectively free of debt, other than a $12k bank obligation in Europe.

About BIO-key International, Inc. (www.BIO-key.com)

BIO-key is a global provider of biometric-centric Identity and Access Management (IAM) and authentication solutions, securing access for over forty million users across government, defense, financial services and enterprise customers. Its PortalGuard IAM platform, Identity-Bound Biometrics and FIDO-certified Passkey:YOU authentication give organizations flexible phoneless, tokenless and passwordless options to secure access to computers, applications, information and high-value transactions, whether cloud-hosted or on-premise.
